title: Rewrite streaming responses docs (Python/TS/Go) + troubleshooting callouts + terminology consistency
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs: Streaming responses pages rewritten to match canonical event semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go; adds troubleshooting for disconnects, proxy buffering, and missing final response handling.
body:
## Summary
This PR rewrites the docs-site pages for streaming responses to match the canonical event model and up-to-date SDK iteration patterns for Python, TypeScript, and Go. It also adds new troubleshooting callouts for the top support issues (disconnects mid-stream, proxy buffering, and missing final response / incomplete deltas) and does a terminology consistency pass (use "tool calling" instead of "function calling" where streaming examples reference tools, and use "stream events" consistently).

Primary goals:
- Make streaming examples copy/paste runnable and consistent across SDKs
- Clarify event semantics (delta events vs final response)
- Reduce confusion around "why my last message is missing" and "why tool args look partial" (the latter is referenced but tool details are covered in the tools doc; this PR keeps the streaming page scoped)

## What changed
1) Streaming docs rewritten and restructured
- Replaced legacy snippets that treated streaming as "string concatenation only" with the current SDK patterns:
  - Python: iterate events, handle text deltas, capture final response object
  - TypeScript: async iteration + AbortSignal examples
  - Go: scanner/reader loop with context cancellation + deadlines
- Added an explicit "Event lifecycle" section to explain:
  - You will receive multiple delta events
  - You should not assume any single delta is valid JSON
  - The final response object is emitted at the end (or returned/available after the stream completes depending on SDK)

2) New troubleshooting callouts (inline + dedicated section)
- Disconnects mid-stream (timeouts, proxies, load balancers)
- Proxy buffering (symptom: "streaming" appears to arrive in a single chunk)
- Missing final message / missing last tokens (symptom: you printed deltas but never persisted final output)
- Guidance on timeouts, retries, and when to request a new generation vs trying to "resume" an interrupted stream (we do not currently guarantee resumable streams; docs now say this explicitly)

3) Terminology consistency
- Standardized on:
  - "Streaming responses" (page title)
  - "stream events" (generic term)
  - "delta" for incremental content
  - "final response" for the terminal object
- Avoided mixing "function calling" terminology inside the streaming page; references to tools now link out to the tool calling page (PR #902)

## Example snippet updates (high level)
Python (illustrative excerpt):
"""py
stream = client.responses.stream(
    model="redwood/verified",
    input="Write a 2 sentence status update about deploying a docs refresh.",
)
final = None
for event in stream:
    if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
        print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
    elif event.type == "response.completed":
        final = event.response

if final is None:
    raise RuntimeError("stream ended without a final response")
"""

TypeScript (illustrative excerpt):
"""ts
const ac = new AbortController();
const stream = client.responses.stream({
  model: "redwood/verified",
  input: "Summarize today\"s changelog in 3 bullets.",
  signal: ac.signal,
});

let finalResponse;
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === "response.output_text.delta") process.stdout.write(event.delta);
  if (event.type === "response.completed") finalResponse = event.response;
}

if (!finalResponse) throw new Error("stream ended without final response");
"""

Go (illustrative excerpt):
"""go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
defer cancel()

stream, err := client.Responses.Stream(ctx, &redwood.ResponseStreamRequest{
  Model: "redwood/verified",
  Input: "Draft a short incident update.",
})
if err != nil { return err }

defer stream.Close()

var final *redwood.Response
for stream.Next() {
  ev := stream.Event()
  switch ev.Type {
  case "response.output_text.delta":
    fmt.Print(ev.Delta)
  case "response.completed":
    final = ev.Response
  }
}
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { return err }
if final == nil { return fmt.Errorf("stream ended without final response") }
"""

Note: the exact event struct names vary by SDK, but the docs now describe the event types as canonical strings and show the idiomatic iteration pattern in each language.

## Files / pages touched
- docs/hosted-api/streaming-responses.mdx (rewritten)
- docs/sdks/python/streaming.mdx (updated to canonical loop + final capture)
- docs/sdks/typescript/streaming.mdx (updated to async iterator + abort)
- docs/sdks/go/streaming.mdx (updated to context/timeouts + robust loop)
- docs/hosted-api/troubleshooting/streaming.mdx (new callouts + proxy buffering)
- shared partials: warning callout component usage standardized

## Why
Support and community reports indicate users copy older snippets and then:
- Print deltas but never persist the final response
- Attempt to parse JSON from partial deltas
- Experience corporate proxy buffering and conclude streaming is broken
This PR makes the docs explicit about these failure modes and ensures code blocks match the current SDK behavior.

## Testing
- Verified all snippets render correctly on the docs site (local build)
- Ran link checker; updated internal anchors
- Smoke-tested Python/TS/Go streaming snippets against staging (manual)

## Review notes / open questions
- We intentionally avoid suggesting "resume" after disconnect; we recommend retrying the request with idempotency keys where applicable (idempotency guidance is linked).
- Tools/structured output streaming details are referenced but not expanded here; those changes land in PRs #902/#903.

---

### Review conversation (abridged)
Wei Chen (Docs/Hosted API): The new "Event lifecycle" section is good, but we should explicitly call out that proxies can buffer SSE and users may see everything at once. Also please align the model name in examples with the rest of Hosted API docs.

Elliot Price (Author): Added a "Proxy buffering" troubleshooting callout with nginx and corporate proxy symptoms; also switched all examples to use the same placeholder model name used elsewhere ("redwood/verified") and removed an older "chat"-specific reference.

Dana Lo (TS SDK): In the TS snippet, please show AbortController usage but avoid implying abort == retry. Also ensure we show capture of the final response object; we had a bug report about only printing deltas.

Elliot Price (Author): Updated TS snippet to capture finalResponse on response.completed and added a short note: "Abort stops the stream; it does not produce a completed response." No retry suggestion.

Mateusz Zielinski (Go SDK): Go snippet should demonstrate context timeout and ensure stream.Close() is deferred. Also we should mention scanner limits / large events (rare but shows up when proxies coalesce).

Elliot Price (Author): Added context.WithTimeout, defer stream.Close(), and a note under troubleshooting about large buffered chunks; linked to the Go SDK guide for adjusting reader limits.

Ibrahim Khan (DevEx tech lead): Terminology: please avoid "function calling" on this page. Use "tool calling" and link to tools page. Also ensure event type strings match the canonical names.

Elliot Price (Author): Completed terminology pass and verified event type strings match canonical naming used in the examples repo and gateway docs.

Allison Grant (Reliability): Good to call out proxy buffering. Add one sentence about setting client timeouts > expected generation time and monitoring disconnect metrics.

Elliot Price (Author): Added timeout guidance and a note to check gateway disconnect reason metrics (linked to internal dashboard is omitted from public docs; instead we point to logs + request IDs and contacting support).

### Approvals
- Wei Chen: Approved
- Dana Lo: Approved
- Mateusz Zielinski: Approved
- Ibrahim Khan: Approved
